blocks.text:
I'm noting the ligand's atomic coordinates, which cluster around x -4 to 1, y 18-21, z 6-10, and now scanning the protein structure for nearby residues within that spatial range.

I find GLU A 5's CB is within about 3.7 Å of the ligand's O3 atom, so that residue counts as a contact. Checking LYS A 19 next, its CB and CG atoms sit too far away in the x-direction to qualify. Then testing SER A 21, its OG atom comes out to roughly 3.96 Å from the ligand's S1 atom, just within the 4.0 Å cutoff, so I'm confirming that distance calculation precisely.

I'm also ruling out SER 21's OG against C1 and its CB against S1, both exceeding 4.4 Å. SER A 18's OG is clearly too far away, so I'm moving on to check GLU A 24's atoms next.

Those come back too far in x as well, along with LEU A 17's CD1 and THR A 20's CB. Scanning further through residues with y-coordinates in the 17-21 range, I'm checking MET1, GLU2, and VAL3's beta and gamma carbons against the ligand atoms — most fail on x-distance, but I'm computing VAL3's CG1 distance to sulfur atom S4 to see if it falls under the cutoff.

I continue checking residues 6-19, SER41, GLU24, LYS19's NZ, and ILE22 against the ligand sulfurs, but each fails on some coordinate axis. Now I'm computing SER21's backbone nitrogen distance to S1 to see if it clears the threshold.

That distance works too, so THR20 counts as within range. Checking CA, CB, OG1, and N atoms of THR20 against S1, only CA falls within the 4Å cutoff while the others are too far. Moving on to LYS19's C atom, the distance comes out too large at around 4.55Å, putting it outside range.

Continuing through LYS19's O atom, SER21's CA and C atoms — SER21's CA confirms within range but C doesn't. Now I'm shifting focus to check which residues sit near the opposite end of the structure, around the C4/S4 coordinates.

GLU5's CD and OE2 atoms both fall too far from S4 and C4 to qualify. VAL3's region is also too distant, so I'm moving on to examine GLU2's OE1 atom.

I'm scanning the file systematically for atoms with higher y-coordinates, checking MET1, GLU2, and VAL3 residues one by one. So far none of VAL3's atoms — N, CB, CG1, CG2, or O — are close enough to S4 to be the match.

Checking LYS4 and GLU5 next, none of their atoms come close enough to S4 or its neighbors either, aside from GLU5's CB. It looks like GLU5 only connects through its CB atom, so I'm now checking CB against C3's coordinates to see if that distance works.

Going further out, I'm scanning VAL6, GLU7, GLU9, LEU17, SER18, LYS19, and THR20 for any atoms within range, but most are too far in the x-direction from the reference point to qualify.

Checking GLY23 and GLU24, also too far. SER21's OG and CB atoms do fall within range though, so that residue qualifies alongside THR20. Verifying THR20's CA and O distances confirms they're within 4 Å, and SER21's OG and N atoms are close too, around 3.4-4 Å.

So my candidate list settles on E5, T20, and S21. I'm double-checking LYS19's CG distance one more time to rule it out, then moving to check ILE22 for completeness.

ILE22's N atom is 5.66 Å away, too far to count. That settles the final list.
